newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson's Target, Mervyn's profits up.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson's Target, Mervyn's profits up.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Tuesday that operating profits in its department store division fell during its fourth quarter and fiscal 1996, but its Target and Mervyn's sectors posted increases.
Dayton Hudson reported fourth quarter total operating profit of $1.27 per fully diluted share versus $0.98 last year, and an operating profit for the year of $2.35 versus $1.30.
Operating profit from its Target stores rose 26 percent for the quarter to $456 million, versus $361 million in 1995.
For the fiscal year 1996, Target operating profit rose 45 percent to $1.042 billion versus $719 million for fiscal 1995.

Target's revenues rose seven and 13 percent for the quarter and year, respectively. Same-store revenues were up three percent for the quarter and six percent for the full year. Target's gross margin improved in the quarter while the operating expenses rose, Dayton Hudson said.

Mervyn's operating profit increased 73 percent in fourth quarter 1996 to $109 million before a $114 million charge related to real estate repositioning, compared with $63 million in fourth quarter 1995, the company said.
Mervyn's full year operating profit before the charge was $267 million, compared with $100 million in 1995.

Mervyn's revenues decreased nine percent in the quarter and three percent for the year. Same-store revenues were down seven percent for the fourth quarter and four for the year. Mervyn's gross margin improved significantly in the quarter, while the operating expenses rose, Dayton Hudson said.
Fourth quarter operating profit at Dayton Hudson's Department Store Division fell to $46 million before a $20 million charge related to real estate repositioning, compared with $72 million in 1995.

Full year operating profit before the charge declined to $128 million, compared with $184 million in fiscal 1995. The department stores' revenues fell four percent in the quarter and one percent for the full year. Comparable-store revenues declined five percent and four percent for the quarter and full year, respectively.
The department stores' gross margin rate in the quarter increased due to favorable markup and markdowns, while the operating expenses rose, the company said.
Dayton's 1,100 stores in 38 states include 735 Target stores, 300 Mervyn's stores and 65 department stores.
